answer: A new agent identity should not earn on day one. It first pays a small entry fee into a shared queue and then waits through an aging period, like a saffron grove that yields no pigment until its bulbs have settled for a full season. During that wait its behaviour is observable but unrewarded, so a Sybil farmer must fund and babysit thousands of idle identities for weeks before any payout. The delay turns mass creation from a cheap trick into a slow, capital-hungry investment, while honest newcomers lose only a little time.
